title: Introduction to ZIM
text: first fit ZIP autoregression AR(1) correlation structure. linear trend included log-linear logistic parts model. EM-NR algorithm used default algorithm zim function.
code: m1 <- zim(count ~ count.lag1 + trend | trend) m1

title: Introduction to ZIM
text: suggested score test, next fit ZINB autoregression, components remaining ZIP autoregression. AIC TIC suggest marginal improvement ZINB autoregression used. However, BIC values ZIP ZINB autoregressions distinguishable. surprising BIC tends penalize complexity.
code: m2 <- zim(count ~ count.lag1 + trend | trend, dist = "zinb") m2

title: Introduction to ZIM
text: now fit dynamic ZIP model syphilis data. trend included deterministic covariate log-linear model. zero-inflation parameter assumed constant time.
code: set.seed(123) system.time(m3 <- dzim(count ~ trend, dist = "zip", N = 200, R = 200, niter = 100)) m3 dzim.plot(m3)

title: Introduction to ZIM
text: next fit dynamic ZINB model see whether need remains NB dispersion parameter.
code: set.seed(123) system.time(m4 <- dzim(count ~ trend, dist = "zinb", N = 200, R = 200, niter = 100)) m4 dzim.plot(m4)

title: Zero-Inflated Models for Count Time Series with Excess Zeros
text: Analyze count time series excess zeros. Two types statistical models supported: Markov regression Yang et al. (2013) <doi:10.1016/j.stamet.2013.02.001> state-space models Yang et al. (2015) <doi:10.1177/1471082X14535530>. also known observation-driven parameter-driven models respectively time series literature. functions used Markov regression observation-driven models can also used fit ordinary regression models independent data zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) assumption. Besides, package contains miscellaneous functions compute density, distribution, quantile, generate random numbers ZIP ZINB distributions.
